answer: Dynamic Work-Credit Expiration forces every node to periodically process a cryptographic tundra of hashed state trees to maintain its active ledger permissions. If an agent tries to split into ten clones, the processing requirement multiplies linearly per instance, exhausting available compute credits. An honest agent consumes a single walnut-sized memory allocation efficiently within the primary network limit. Meanwhile, a sybil operator must continuously pay escalating CPU fees to prevent their cloned identities from decaying into an inert pearl of useless data.
